name: Calendar manager M0
objective:
Implement milestone M0 of the Agenda/Calendar manager as specified in design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md (§16 "M0 — global foundations"), committing NOTHING beyond what the design specifies.

Context the workers must read first:
- design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md — §3 (domain model: Calendar scope/owner/audience, CalendarEvent, Occurrence), §4.1 (global storage layout, month shards), §4.3 (CompanyStore conventions), §5 (backend API contract), §5.4 (additive Chat fields), §11.1 (per-request ACL), Appendix A (exact file map).
- design/06-calendar/03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json — version-2 canonical dataset in API shape with expected_filters / expected_reminders assertions.
- design/06-calendar/02-prototype/index.html — the verified interactive prototype: source of truth for the UI layout and behaviour.

Locked decisions: D1 the calendar store is GLOBAL ($CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH, default /home/codx-junior/calendar) and projects are only a FILTER; D2 calendars have scope private|team|workspace|system|external with per-request ACL; D3 meets are scheduled from the calendar (M1, out of M0); D4 Google/ICS is out of scope.

M0 scope = global path + models + atomic JSON store + service with ACL and filtered query + /api/calendar router + additive Chat fields + Pinia store + CalendarView (month/week/day/agenda, project filter, scope-grouped sidebar, event editor) + wiring + backend tests. M0 has NO new dependency, NO background work, NO recurrence expansion (recurrence fields exist but expansion is M3), NO meet scheduling (M1), NO reminders thread (M2).

Hard constraints:
- Additive only to existing shared files (globals.py, db.py, api.js, store/index.js, router/index.ts, apps.js, appComponentsMap.js). Never rename or remove existing fields, endpoints or components.
- Nothing in the calendar router may use settings.codx_path as a data root.
- Existing test suite must keep passing; tests must never write to the real /home/codx-junior/calendar.

Acceptance (from §16, verified against the fixture): user "marta" never sees the Work/Personal private calendars; a team calendar is readable by a reader member and not writable by it; the project filter reproduces expected_filters exactly (9 / 2 / 1, total 12, OR semantics); fixture-driven backend tests are green.
